admitted.text: She seems to have survived being seen on the bench by sealing herself back behind her face, and she decided it would be for good.
admitted.detail_quote: He could have the face. The face was very good. The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: Being seen by Pace seems to frighten her as much as she needs it.
admitted.detail_quote: It makes me feel real. And some nights it frightens me.

admitted.text: Randi seems to use performance as armor whenever genuine need threatens to become visible.
admitted.detail_quote: Nothing ever happened to her. That was what the face was for.

admitted.text: At brunch she reads as a skilled handler who draws Vee's secrets out and then shuts the door at the moment that suits her.
admitted.detail_quote: For the threesome. For when she's ready. Somebody has to get her used to my mouth.

admitted.text: She can also seem truly generous to Vee, turning Vee's shame into permission.
admitted.detail_quote: The heart on her, Pace. She doesn't do anything halfway.

admitted.text: Her jealousy of Pace's unhurried time with Vee seems to have turned bitter.
admitted.detail_quote: You've got her all weekend, every weekend, and you're in no hurry, and I can't think why you would be.

admitted.text: Finding Vee's panties in Pace's drawer reads as grief she cannot name, which she covers by acting.
admitted.detail_quote: She had put his hands on her before, but never there.

admitted.text: She seems to want Vee for herself, not only "for us," and catches herself admitting it.
admitted.detail_quote: I didn't think I'd like her this much. I keep waiting to get bored of her — I get bored of everybody — and it doesn't come.

admitted.text: Her father's PPP fraud seems to strike her as a fresh, personal betrayal, not something she already knew.
admitted.detail_quote: Randi's face was doing very little, and the very little was the whole of it. The color had gone out of it.

admitted.text: He reads as truly committed to consent, the principle he will not bend.
admitted.detail_quote: She chooses it, Randi. Every step of it. Or it isn't anything.

admitted.text: Pace reads as deeply attentive, making care concrete through food, warmth, craft, and precisely limited touch.
admitted.detail_quote: She chooses it, Randi. Every step of it. Or it isn't anything.

admitted.text: Under the courtliness there is real appetite; he picked Vee for himself as much as for Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: or that he had never once pointed at a woman he did not want.

admitted.text: Pace seems capable of reading bodies more fluently than spoken emotional needs.
admitted.detail_quote: He took it for the want — too big for her, come down on him with nowhere else to go.

admitted.text: He seems to defend his teenage relationship with Daphne without hearing that he is defending it.
admitted.detail_quote: That he had handed her the thing that had hurt him and named it luck.

admitted.text: He seems to answer love with love's outline while holding back the word itself.
admitted.detail_quote: He'd given her all of it and not the name.

admitted.text: His discomfort in loud rooms reads as a real sensory limit, not a rejection of Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: In a room like that I listen as hard as I know how and I still can't hear you. Somewhere quieter, I can.

admitted.text: Pace seems disturbingly comfortable preserving the deception so long as Vee freely chooses each visible step.
admitted.detail_quote: So when she came out of those doors with her head thrown all the way back, laughing, I knew. I pointed at her and watched your face.

admitted.text: Her desire and her shame seem tied together, yet she is learning to burn through the shame.
admitted.detail_quote: The voice said floozie in her mother's exact word and her thighs pressed once, hard, on their own

admitted.text: Vee seems to experience Pace’s attention as permission to discover rather than suppress her appetites.
admitted.detail_quote: She had spent the entire afternoon being seen at her most ashamed and had not, once, been found wanting.

admitted.text: She seems to explain away Randi's kisses so she doesn't have to see her own desire.
admitted.detail_quote: except that this time, when it should have ended, Vee was the one who wouldn't let it, leaning up the last half-inch after Randi

admitted.text: She reads as fiercely proud about money, and the pride costs her.
admitted.detail_quote: Vee laid the debit card on her own folder and felt the little familiar drop as she let go of it

admitted.text: She seems unable to rest without a name for what she and Pace are.
admitted.detail_quote: She had no name for the best thing in her life, not the big one he wouldn't give her and not the small one she couldn't find

admitted.text: Vee's mother seems to have planted the shame that speaks inside Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: the word arriving whole and in her mother's voice before she had finished forming the picture.

admitted.text: She seems wary of Randi from the start and watches what Vee misses.
admitted.detail_quote: Cassie was watching Randi thumb at her phone, her own pencil stopped in her hand.

admitted.text: She reads as deeply loyal, someone who cares about Vee and not the glamour.
admitted.detail_quote: The whole forty seconds Vee had spent being a student, Cassie had spent watching what the dress had done to her friend

admitted.text: Brooke reads as a warm, watchful power who files what she learns.
admitted.detail_quote: Brooke was the chapter president and did not need to stand to stop someone in her own common room.

admitted.text: Sheri reads as a frank, clear-eyed friend who sees the trouble coming.
admitted.detail_quote: If that's not already complicated, it will be. But I bet it's worth it.

admitted.text: Meg seems to be the steady, mildly skeptical voice.
admitted.detail_quote: Everybody's different at the start.

admitted.text: Kayla reads as an excited cheerleader who sees what Pace's invitation means.
admitted.detail_quote: We're doing hair Saturday. I'm coming to your room. This is happening.

admitted.text: Looked at from outside, Daphne reads as an adult who took on a child's care and then his love.
admitted.detail_quote: an older student, to help the child find his feet.

admitted.text: The bench: Pace's craft built for exposure, waiting for Vee as it once waited for Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: full of what it was, doing what it would continue to do, waiting for the next time.

admitted.text: the bench hidden beneath the table: desire and power concealed inside ordinary domestic surfaces
admitted.detail_quote: Tomorrow he would put the top back on and the bench would be a long table again

admitted.text: The key in a lock: Randi's self locking shut, echoed later when Randi's words open Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: the size of a key turning in a lock.

admitted.text: thin apple slices: appetite portioned into an acceptable form before Pace begins feeding what Randi denies
admitted.detail_quote: a girl who had been portioning herself, weighing every want before she let herself have it

admitted.text: "Latent variables": the hidden factor driving what Vee sees.
admitted.detail_quote: the word sat there in her notebook, underlined once, going nowhere

admitted.text: the right-angle substitution: separate people or desires becoming legible only when combined
admitted.detail_quote: Put them together, at right angles, and they turn into a single thing that's suddenly plain

admitted.text: the water: a private self beyond judgment where Vee’s body belongs to her again
admitted.detail_quote: Nobody up there could see her. Nobody down here wanted anything.

admitted.text: the outlier: a hidden family corruption that can be isolated statistically but not emotionally
admitted.detail_quote: the biggest one, off on its own in the white

admitted.text: the green satin pressed between Randi's palm and his chest: reads as the two women's bodies meeting in one object, the triangle made flesh without Vee present
admitted.detail_quote: She had pressed Vee between them this morning, and it had excited her as much as it fired him now.

admitted.text: The bathroom drawer: Pace saying love through what he does rather than what he says.
admitted.detail_quote: He hadn't told her it didn't matter. He'd gone and made her a place instead.

admitted.text: The flannel shirt: Vee's need to carry Pace's presence, which fades and has to be renewed.
admitted.detail_quote: She'd carry it away Sunday full of him, and sleep in him through the nights that weren't his, and bring it back gone faint again to be filled.

admitted.text: the burgundy silk: being known more exactly than one’s stated wish
admitted.detail_quote: He hadn't matched the dress she'd described. He'd matched *her.*

admitted.text: the dress’s slit: Vee’s choice to turn exposure into authorship
admitted.detail_quote: She took a breath, and made the second step long.

admitted.text: Crackers and a meal: Vee's hunger for love put into the language of food.
admitted.detail_quote: I had been eating crackers my whole life," she said. "And you fed me a meal.

admitted.text: The Chili's nachos: an old "fine" that Pace has spoiled for good.
admitted.detail_quote: He had ruined it for her, was the thing. Not just this.

admitted.text: The glaze on Vee's lip: Randi's kiss leaving a trace of an appetite Vee never touched.
admitted.detail_quote: there was a thread of sweetness, sugar and butter and something warm under it, the glaze of a pastry she had never once touched.

admitted.text: When and how will Vee learn that Randi and Pace selected her together?
admitted.detail_quote: She consents — every time — or I'm done.

admitted.text: Will Pace ever say he loves Vee?
admitted.detail_quote: I love how good we are together.

admitted.text: What will Vee call Pace, to herself and to her parents?
admitted.detail_quote: She had no name for the best thing in her life

admitted.text: What is the scar on Pace's inner thigh?
admitted.detail_quote: the not-tonight had no wall in it, only a door with a time on it that wasn't now.

admitted.text: What happened between Pace and his parents?
admitted.detail_quote: I don't go back.

admitted.text: Where does Randi's accent come from, and why does it get stronger when she's moved?
admitted.detail_quote: Randi had something in her mouth that wasn't from anywhere near here — the esses ran a half-beat long, and the a's came up arched and lifted

admitted.text: What did Pace’s relationship with Daphne truly involve, and what does he still misunderstand about it?
admitted.detail_quote: Daphne had built a door, once, and he had not respected it.

admitted.text: What will Randi do with the discovery of her father’s apparent fraud?
admitted.detail_quote: The point opened into a record and the record opened into a name, and the first word of the name was MIRANDA.

admitted.text: Is Randi falling in love with Vee, with Pace, or with both?
admitted.detail_quote: I went to come off her and she came after me.

admitted.text: Can Randi confess that her desire for Vee has become her own before jealousy turns that desire cruel?
admitted.detail_quote: God, I want her.
